messages:
alex.k: Heads-up — seeing a gradual ECC uptick across GPUs in rack44, started late last night. Not full failures but single-bit counts climbing and occasional Xid noise.
monitoring-bot: :warning: ALERT rack44 GPU ECC rate > 3x baseline for 4h. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/metrics/rack44
maria.p: Pulling NVML dumps from affected nodes. Can we freeze new heavy jobs on rack44 until we triage? Ill mark it as `drain-needed` in the fleet console.
sam.t: Ack — placing soft-scheduling hold for rack44 and draining non-critical pods. Moving queued batches to other racks now.
jin.z: Quick tail from node-r44-03 syslog — repeating PCIe link resets and Xid 31. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T23:12:02Z] nvml: GPU 3 ECC single-bit 124 -> 146
[2026-03-17T23:12:03Z] nvml: Xid 31 on GPU 3 (pcie link reset)
[2026-03-17T23:12:03Z] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Root port reported RX_ERR
```
alex.k: Thanks jin. Cross-referencing asset DB: 6 nodes in rack44 share serial prefix `A8X4B-` (vendor lot tag). Those cards were received Nov 2025.
vendor-eng: Confirmed — lot A8X4B shipped 2025-11. Weve seen similar symptoms in small internal runs: thermal cycling -> micro-solder delamination causing intermittent link issues. Firmware on those units is 1.2.3. Were pushing FW 1.2.4 which reduces link re-negotiation frequency; long-term fix may be RMA for affected serials.
maria.p: Proposed containment: drain & memtest nodes with ECC delta > 100 in 7d OR Xid > 5. Estimated 7 nodes across rack44 and adjacent top-of-rack. Draft runbook:
1) cordon node: `kubectl cordon node-r44-0{1,2,3}`
2) drain: `kubectl drain node-r44-0X --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3) run memtest: `gpu-memtest --passes 3 --log /tmp/memtest.log`
4) collect NVML: `nvml-tool dump --csv /tmp/nvml-node-r44-0X.csv`
5) if memtest/NVML indicate failures -> schedule RMA and replace node/gpu
sam.t: Logistics/cost note: on-site reflow + FW update can be attempted first (vendor shipped tech), turnaround ~1 business day. Full RMA+swap is 3–5 business days and we lose ~48 GPU-days if we block nodes during swaps. I can model capacity impact in the hourly cost dashboard.
alex.k: Risk tolerance: if Xid flaps continue after FW roll, prefer full RMA. For now: schedule vendor tech for FW reflow on Monday, run memtests this weekend. Jin, can you run the memtest pass tonight and attach NVML dumps?
jin.z: On it. Will run memtest on node-r44-01..04 tonight and drop logs in /shared/infra/triage/rack44/
maria.p: I created INF-4821 with serial list, NVML links, and a short postmortem template: https://internal.tickets/INF-4821 :clipboard:
vendor-eng: Well prepare an RMA SOW for the A8X4B lot and include optional on-site reflow + FW 1.2.4 push. If you want to try FW first we can queue tech for Mon AM.
sam.t: I'll update the autoscaler to avoid burst placing new jobs on rack44 until remediation complete. Also adding capacity buffer +10% to the pooling algorithm.
monitoring-bot: Note: temporary alert mute applied for rack44 to avoid noise while we run memtests. Alerts still recorded in incident log.
alex.k: Action items recap: maria -> INF-4821 + coordinate on-site tech; jin -> memtests + NVML dumps; sam -> capacity plan + scheduler hold; vendor-eng -> RMA SOW & FW artifact. Target remediation window: EOD Fri (soft), full RMA complete within 5 business days if needed.
maria.p: Will follow up with a short postmortem after node-level results. Early hypothesis: bad batch (A8X4B) + thermal cycles accelerating micro-solder cracks -> PCIe re-negotiation -> ECC drift and Xid spikes. :mag:
sam.t: Thx all. If memtests are clean after FW reflow we can avoid full RMA. If not, prep for swaps and let ops know when to book racks with facilities.
alex.k: Good thread. Please add any logs to the ticket and ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
